_: THE SOURCE REGISTRY FOR THE SETUP CATALOG. Every number in setup_criteria.json cites one or more ids from here, and every id here points at something that RESOLVES: a URL, a book with a chapter, a firm store with a selector, or a firm code location. Research artifact only — nothing reads this file.
_grounding_rule: The owner's decision EXTENDS THE SOURCES, NOT THE DISCIPLINE. An external citation is legitimate grounding IF IT RESOLVES. What stays forbidden is an invented number. So a source with `resolved: verified` was fetched and its quote read back in this pass; `resolved: reported` was read by a research agent but not re-fetched by the compiler; `resolved: blocked` could not be opened at all and anything citing it is LOW confidence by construction.
_no_average: WHERE SOURCES DISAGREE, EVERY ONE OF THEM IS REGISTERED AND EVERY NUMBER IS KEPT. Nothing here is averaged. An average is a number nobody published, which is the exact defect the grounding rule exists to prevent. The disagreements are indexed in SETUP_NOTES.md section 6.

_kinds.firm_code: a firm code location that resolves by AST — module + symbol. The kind conceptVocabulary.json already calls `classifier`.
_kinds.firm_preset: a labelled threshold in api/services/screener/filters.py::FILTERS. The kind conceptVocabulary.json calls `filter_preset`.
_kinds.firm_screen: a shipped screen in api/services/screener/saved_screens.py::starters(). The kind conceptVocabulary.json calls `starter_screen`.
_kinds.firm_playbook: the firm's authored prose in app/src/pages/modelbook/setupPlaybooks.js. ⛔ A PLAYBOOK IS NEVER A GROUNDING — it is prose and cannot mechanically produce a tree. It rides as an ATTRIBUTION, per starterScans.json::_grounding.

duncan_hvc.note: ⭐ THE ORIGINATOR OF HVC, publishing a full numeric spec on his own site — and the setup the firm currently refuses turns out to be one of the best-sourced available. Companion: gregduncan.feather.blog/3-best-trading-setups. Not an O'Neil/Minervini/IBD construct; no such attribution exists.

zarattini_orb_stocks.authors: Carlo Zarattini, Andrea Barbon, Andrew Aziz
zarattini_orb_stocks.title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market
zarattini_orb_stocks.note: ⭐ THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE CITATION IN THE INTRADAY FAMILY. >7,000 US stocks, 2016-2023, survivorship-bias free, read in full. Publishes the universe screen, the exact time-of-day-matched RelativeVolume formula, and the 5/15/30/60-minute comparison in which the 30-minute range is the WORST (Sharpe 0.21 vs 2.81).

zarattini_orb_qqq.title: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable?
zarattini_orb_qqq.note: The original 5-minute ORB spec on QQQ/TQQQ: entry at the second candle's open, doji = no trade, stop at the first candle's low, target 10R, 1% risk, 4x leverage cap.

zarattini_vwap.title: VWAP: The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems
zarattini_vwap.note: ⭐ THE ONLY RIGOROUS NUMERIC VWAP RULES ANYWHERE. VWAP = sum(HLC x Vol)/sum(Vol), RTH only; entry at exactly 9:31:00 ET; and the operational definition of losing VWAP: exit ONLY on a 1-minute candle CLOSE through it.

zarattini_gap.title: The Power Of Price Action Reading
zarattini_gap.note: 🔴 THE FINDING THAT CONTRADICTS THE EDUCATOR CONSENSUS. Screen: open >= 6% above the prior close, price >= $2, >= 200,000 shares pre-market — 9,794 events, 2016-2023. Buying every one at 9:30 with no stop is -0.25R by day 8. The strategy only turns positive with selection + a 10-SMA trail + 25% partials at 2R/4R/8R/10R.

connors_stts.title: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (TradingMarkets, 2008), ch. 9, 11, 12 and 15
connors_stts.note: ⭐ RSI(2) < 5 with a 200-day trend filter, exit above the 5-period MA — verified against the book text, and immediately expressible because `rsi` takes an explicit period. ⚠️ The SHORT-side thresholds (95/90) could NOT be corroborated in the book; attribute those to StockCharts.

crabel_tasc_1988.author: Toby Crabel
crabel_tasc_1988.title: Playing the Opening Range Breakout Part 1
crabel_tasc_1988.publication: Technical Analysis of STOCKS & COMMODITIES V.6:9 (Sept 1988), pp. 337-339
crabel_tasc_1988.note: ⭐ THE ONE PRIMARY CRABEL SOURCE REACHED. The Stretch = the 10-day average of min(High-Open, Open-Low); orders at Open +/- Stretch. ⛔ HIS ORIGINAL USES NO INTRADAY RANGE AT ALL — Zarattini's own literature review confirms it. Every Crabel PERFORMANCE number in circulation is a third-party backtest.

oxfordstrat_oops.title: Oops pattern — parameterised backtest
oxfordstrat_oops.note: Gives the entry unambiguously (buy stop AT yesterday's LOW, not the close) and records 'Filters: None specified' for gap size. Their own test grades it D.

chartist_oops.author: Nick Radge
chartist_oops.title: The Oops bailout decomposition
chartist_oops.note: 🔴 THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE DECOMPOSITION IN THE CATALOG: same entry, 98.6% win rate with the bailout exit (win/loss ratio 0.05, average loser held 59 days) vs 50.5% without it (ratio 1.36). Also: 88% in-sample 1987-1998 vs 58.9% out-of-sample 1998-2015.

owltrader_ur.publisher: The Owl Trader (Gil Morales / Dr. Chris Kacher lineage)
owltrader_ur.title: Undercut & Rally
owltrader_ur.note: ⭐ Establishes the provenance (Morales/Kacher, NOT IBD) and states that a point-based undercut tolerance is deliberately withheld as 'arbitrary and imprecise'.

talib_source.title: TA-Lib C source — ta_CDLHAMMER.c, ta_CDLKICKING.c, ta_global.c, ta_utility.h
talib_source.note: ⭐ READ FROM SOURCE, so it is the one fully unambiguous candle specification available. Its candle-settings table (BodyLong RealBody/10/1.0, BodyDoji HighLow/10/0.1, ShadowVeryShort HighLow/10/0.1, Near HighLow/5/0.2 …) is the third measurement BASIS in the wick problem, and it is far stricter than every textbook rule.

taplot_wickplay.title: TAPLOT Wick Play (attributed to Oliver Kell)
taplot_wickplay.note: The only place the Wick Play's three-bar structure is written down. ⛔ NO numeric threshold anywhere in it — the settings are 'configurable' with no published defaults.

firm_kb_pattern_calibration.title: The firm's 16-setup identification matrix
firm_kb_pattern_calibration.note: Per-setup 'critical differentiator' with numbers, plus a 'most confused with' for each. The firm's own disambiguation layer.

rejected._: WHAT WAS EXAMINED AND NOT USED, AND WHY. Recorded because a catalog that only lists what it kept is a list of what somebody remembered — and because three of these are numbers in wide circulation with NO author behind them, which is precisely the failure the grounding rule exists to catch.

no_author_owned_source.why_rejected: NO Qullamaggie-owned page states an ADR floor. His own pages use ADR only to CAP STOP WIDTH ('if the ADR of the stock is 5%, your stop shouldn't be wider than 5%') — which is a different claim entirely. Community folklore until an authored source appears. ⚠️ The firm's own brain templates repeat 'ADR% 4-5%+' as a requirement; that inherits the same problem.

no_author_owned_source.claim: Dan Zanger's volume ratios (ZVR >= 1.5x / 1.65x / 2x), 'close in the upper 25% of the bar', 'don't chase >5% above the breakout'
no_author_owned_source.why_rejected: chartpattern.com's own pages carry none of these numbers. Not treated as Zanger's published rules.
The RDT wiki index was read in full and contains no numbers beyond a claimed win rate and a learning-time estimate. Do not attribute a generic RVOL threshold to them.

login_or_bot_walled._note: ⛔ Nothing was signed into, no credentials were entered, and the two CAPTCHAs were abandoned rather than solved. The one X post used was read from a search index's reproduction of its text, never from X.

bulk_rejections._worst_example: A search summary asserted that Pradeep Bonde is 'known as @traderstewie'. That is false — @stockbee is Pradeep Bonde and @traderstewie is a different person. Everything downstream of that conflation was dropped.

counts._: Counted, not estimated. 'Examined' = a distinct URL either fetched or triaged on title + indexed snippet. Two sweeps are merged here; four more were dispatched and are recorded in SETUP_NOTES.md section 9.
counts._shortfall: 🔴 THE ~1,000-SOURCE TARGET WAS NOT MET AND THE REASON IS MECHANICAL, NOT EDITORIAL. The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) and subagent budget (200/200) were both exhausted mid-run. The second sweep planned a six-way domain partition and had to collapse it into one sequential thread; the first lost the ability to route around blocked hosts. Roughly 275 distinct sources were examined across the two merged sweeps. What is DEEP: Bulkowski, StockCharts ChartSchool, Qullamaggie, Stockbee, TraderLion, and the Lo-Mamaysky-Wang primary paper. What is THIN OR ABSENT: IBD/investors.com (host-blocked), Investopedia (host-blocked), the textbook layer (Edwards & Magee, Kirkpatrick & Dahlquist, the CMT curriculum), broker education (Fidelity/Recognia, Schwab, IBKR), and the screener vendors (official TC2000, Finviz, Trade Ideas, TrendSpider). ⭐ A fresh session with raised search/subagent caps would close those three lanes, and that is where the remaining value is.
